title: Jimmy Johnson, Bolden and Kenny's Hall
summary: He covers Jimmy Johnson, who played with Bolden, Jack Carey and the Crescent Band, and substituting for him at Kenny's Hall, a dance hall used as a church on Sundays, with that band's lineup.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Jimmy, Jimmy, Jimmy Johnson, yeah, I used to sing. Oh, sure, we all met him. Sure. Of course. Jimmy Johnson, well, he played all right. He used to play with Jack Carey, you know. He played with the Crescent Band, you know. I love the Crescent Band. Yeah, and before he played with the Crescent Band, he used to play with, um. Play with Bolden. Buddy Bolden. Buddy Bolden.
Did you ever hear Bolden's band, that's one year?

Oh, yeah, Buddy Bolden's band. You played with him? Sure, I played with Jimmy, sure, and Jimmy. Jimmy used to work in some, uh, factory, you know. Factory, yeah. See? Bunch of factory. That's right. And lots of time, you know, he'd be late if he couldn't make it, and I used to pitch it for him. Yeah. He was playing at a hall on Padilla and Liberty called, uh, Kenny's Hall. Oh, yeah. You remember that, Kenny's Hall? That's a good one. I don't know.
I used to call it funky butthole. That's it.
I took a picture of it.
I took a picture of it.
That's all night, Saturday night or Sunday morning, and then twenty minutes after it'd be a church.
They turned it into a church, finally got a steeple on it, and church windows, you know.

Well, that's what it was after we, old man, old man all the time. But you'd play a dance and then they'd have church on Sunday. Yeah, you'd play Saturday night, they'd dance there, and see. They used it for church? And they used it for Sunday for the church. Oh, I didn't know that. Old man Kenny would own the place. Then the outfathers hall was running down there on Padilla and the ramparts. Padilla and the Rampart. Smith was at that. Yeah, and Kenny's Hall was on Liberty and Padilla. Different class of people. It was awful. Yeah, and Buddy Bowling used to play in there. I can tell you, every band played in a band.

Buddy Bowling, trumpet. A fella named Frank played clarinet. Frank Lewis. Frank Lewis. Frank Lewis. All right, old Connish played trombone. Willie Connish played trombone. Jimmy Johnson played bass. And his name was Lewis? No, Jimmy Phillips.
Yeah. Jimmy Phillips. Or Lewis was the clarinet.

Yeah. That's the way that was. Then Vien, Vien taking his place after that. Well, you remember when D.D. played with? D.D. Yeah, D.D. Channel. Yeah. Remember when D.D. played with? Sure. Yeah. And they had Frank Duesen. Even John Vien played with him, too. John Vien played with him after? After, yeah. And all the good drummers.
